issue_context.title: New Ecobee Premium model not recognized
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Added the new Ecobee Premium to Home Assistant and got the following error in the logs:
---------------
Logger: homeassistant.components.ecobee
Source: components/ecobee/climate.py:182
Integration: ecobee ([documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/ecobee), [issues](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22integration%3A+ecobee%22))
First occurred: May 21, 2022, 4:05:40 PM (4 occurrences)
Last logged: May 21, 2022, 7:08:49 PM

Model number for ecobee thermostat Downstairs not recognized. Please visit this link to open a new issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues and include the following information: Unrecognized model number: aresSmart
Model number for ecobee thermostat Upstairs not recognized. Please visit this link to open a new issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues and include the following information: Unrecognized model number: aresSmart
---------------

Three notes:
1. The thermostats due appear to work in HA regardless of the error. 
2. This model does have features like air quality that aren't found in previous versions, so that would a nice bonus to have as available sensors
3. There is another new model called the Ecobee Enhanced, but I don't have one to report the model number

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

Home Assistant Core 2022.5.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Home Assistant Core 2022.5.2

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Ecobee

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.components.ecobee
Source: components/ecobee/climate.py:182
Integration: ecobee ([documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/ecobee), [issues](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22integration%3A+ecobee%22))
First occurred: May 21, 2022, 4:05:40 PM (4 occurrences)
Last logged: May 21, 2022, 7:08:49 PM

Model number for ecobee thermostat Downstairs not recognized. Please visit this link to open a new issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues and include the following information: Unrecognized model number: aresSmart
Model number for ecobee thermostat Upstairs not recognized. Please visit this link to open a new issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues and include the following information: Unrecognized model number: aresSmart
```

+1 on this; have same issue. For me however, the climate, weather & occupancy sensors show up. Still model "unknown".

As a note, I do see the climate, weather and occupancy sensors, though not the new air quality (which isn't surprising). The Smart Sensors also show up fine, which is great. 

One oddity I did discover since I reported this bug however. While the Smart Sensor's occupancy and temperature sensors show up . . . for example , the following is the Family Room Smart Sensor . . .

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/694386/170814119-6656edaa-2d7a-4c14-92f3-f4c72d440255.png)

. . . the actual humidity and temperature sensors from the thermostat itself (as opposed to the occupancy and the averaged temperature values that Ecobee creates across the sensors) don't properly show in the room they are associated with. Here are some shots of the 'Downstairs' thermostat showing which room it is in (Front Hall), but the humidity/temperature sensors are in the generic sensors section in the Overview Dashboard instead of in the Front Hall, where you can see occupancy sensor and overall thermostat control.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/694386/170814535-184af9fb-3692-4c8b-8b30-ce7b3c547e09.png)
Above shows room the thermostat should be in (the Front Hall)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/694386/170814544-2c139f67-a50a-4894-a5ca-03dd25c3e983.png)
Above shows the occupancy and thermostat control in the Front Hall.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/694386/170814551-5aa5a1ce-f1e0-471f-93c3-8361d94a25bd.png)
Above shows the humidity and temperature in the generic sensor section since the room isn't associated.

This happened for both upstairs and downstairs thermostats.

+1 on this. Just installed my Ecobee Premium today and experiencing the same issue as reported by OP.

Using:

Home Assistant Core 2022.5.5
Home Assistant Supervisor 2022.05.3
Home Assistant OS 8.1

+1 I have the Smart Thermostat Premium. I can use and control it normally within my HA setup; however I cannot see the Air Quality data. Is anyone able to see if the data is exposed by the API, and the integration simply needs an update to map this data?

It looks like Ecobee's own API documentation has not been updated in a couple of years, and doesn't yet list the new models. Without documentation on the new API functions, this will likely need to be reverse engineered.

https://www.ecobee.com/home/developer/api/documentation/v1/change-log.shtml
https://www.ecobee.com/home/developer/api/introduction/core-concepts.shtml#models

Additionally, the following issues appear to be duplicates of this one:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/73717
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/75611
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/75388
Has anyone tried to reach out to Ecobee on the matter? Presumably they published the API documentation in good faith initially, perhaps an update is forthcoming?

Adding the Smart Premium is just a matter of adding another entry to const.py 

The co2 sensors already exist in the API;

[https://www.ecobee.com/home/developer/api/documentation/v1/objects/Sensor.shtml](url)

I’m guessing there’s another sensor type value called voc

+1 - I have 2x Premium Thermostat installed and HA doesn't pull the humidity and air quality. Also it is not showing the model correctly. 
Reading on all these above comments - what needs to take place in order to have the latest devices showing the data correctly into HA ?

> +1 - I have 2x Premium Thermostat installed and HA doesn't pull the humidity and air quality. Also it is not showing the model correctly. 
> 
> Reading on all these above comments - what needs to take place in order to have the latest devices showing the data correctly into HA ?

Humidity should definitely be showing correctly, is working just fine for me
Yeah, humidity works just fine, need CO2 and VOC. :-)

There’s also an AQI sensor in there. 

It’s retrieving the data already, it’s just a matter of putting it into the correct sensor objects. 

Bear with me, it’s slow going since I’ve never written a line of python code in my life :)

Thanks for looking into this!
